page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is supported by a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. Memory capacity is configured at 96.0 GB, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This server includes 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable. The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_tile, AMX_int8), alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_ni.

In benchmark testing, the D48lds_v7 demonstrates strong computational and processing capabilities. It achieved a PassMark CPU score of 66237.87 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 47815.49. Single-threaded gzip compression reached a top-tier score of 36.36 GB/sec, while bzip3 multi-threaded decompression registered at 302.08 GB/sec. For lightweight AI workloads, the server processed 135M model text generation at a top-tier rate of 338.79 tokens/sec.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the server is optimized for compute-heavy tasks rather than memory-intensive applications. This resource allocation provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high clock speeds and parallel processing without the overhead of excess memory. It is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, database operations, and localized data processing tasks that leverage its 2.8 TB local NVMe storage.

The instance features 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. In benchmark evaluations, the server delivered strong performance, including a PassMark CPU score of 66237.87, a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 302.08 GB/sec, and 79.57 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. This configuration is optimized for compute-intensive workloads, database operations, and high-throughput web serving where local high-speed storage is required but massive memory footprints are not.
